page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it features 40 physical cores and 40 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.8 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on external storage solutions and utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the average performance tier across several metrics. The dedicated Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07. In memory operations, the instance records a read-only small block bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, it demonstrates a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 166.28 GB/sec and a Geekbench software compilation score of 28733.0. In database and key-value store tests, the server processes 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14249.04 in Passmark database operations.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge offers a balanced allocation of high-frequency compute power and memory without the added cost of bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require sustained, high-clock CPU performance but do not need local scratch space or hardware-accelerated graphics. However, the lack of local storage means all disk I/O must traverse the network, which may introduce latency compared to instances with local NVMe drives.

This hardware profile is suited for compute-intensive applications, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is also capable of handling moderate machine learning tasks, such as small to medium LLM inference, where it achieves 56.94 tokens/second for prompt processing on a 7B model.
